_note: The Rendering Lab's reproducible configurations. Every one of these is a recipe that already existed -- in docs/quality-lab/README.md's 'Using it' block, in ADR-243 and in ADR-257 -- written down in the one place a case number can be resolved from. Nothing here is a new experiment; it is the existing ones made addressable, which is the whole of spec 32.

cases.title: Aliasing, candidate against its own supersampled reference
cases.question: On the benchmark scene built to alias, how far is a production frame from a better-sampled one of the same second?
cases.expectation: The candidate is measurably worse. This is the arm that must MOVE -- a metric that cannot separate 1x from 2x on a scene of fence slats and a receding tile grid is not measuring sampling.
cases.notes: The reference arm is this case with supersample 2.0 (case 2). --aov and --supersample are refused together (ADR-242), which is why the reference carries no AOVs and why the pair is two cases rather than one.

cases.title: Aliasing, the supersampled reference
cases.question: What does this second of this scene look like when sampling is not the limit?
cases.expectation: Nothing to assert on its own. This case exists to be the other half of case 1, and a report that names it as a reference must carry its sequence hash -- two arms that hash identically are void, not equal.

cases.title: Aliasing dolly, with the AOVs the temporal detectors need
cases.question: Under lateral camera motion, does the motion-compensated residual separate real instability from authored movement?
cases.expectation: The residual stays low while the temporal alternation is large, because the second difference of a translating image is not zero. ADR-243 in miniature: the temporal detector calls authored motion instability and the residual does not.
cases.notes: Two seconds of frames, not one: the temporal detectors have nothing to say about a single frame. Reproduce with --range 0:2 in place of the single-frame range the printed command uses.

cases.title: Aliasing dolly with FXAA removed
cases.question: How much of the spatial measure's reading is FXAA?
cases.expectation: The spatial Laplacian rises with FXAA off. This is a control for case 3, not a quality question: an instrument that does not move when the only antialiasing in the pipe is removed is reading something other than antialiasing.
cases.notes: There is no TAA in this engine. fxaa is the whole antialiasing arm, and removing it is the strongest available.

cases.title: The shadow AOV against the mask the lit pass consumed
cases.question: Does the `shadow` AOV's recomputed visibility term equal the one the lit pass actually used?
cases.expectation: Close and not exact. ADR-258 measured 0.43% of pixels differing, max 22/255 -- so the metric built on it ships labelled an approximation. This case is the arm; case 6 is its control.
cases.notes: `maskconsume` is a diagnostic configuration no tier sets and nothing ships: the shadow mask at full resolution AND consumed. It exists so the comparison has something to compare against -- at `high` and `offline` the engine's own mask is never built.

cases.title: CONTROL for case 5: the shadow atlas halved
cases.question: Does the comparison in case 5 move at all when the shadows genuinely change?
cases.expectation: Both arms move. ADR-258 measured 1.86% inline and 1.93% masked -- four times case 5's disagreement. Without this, 'close' in case 5 is a number with no scale on it.
cases.notes: ADR-182's positive control for case 5, and the reason case 5's finding is a finding.
